notes:
What's new in 0.1.137:
- Log out: if the window stays on the "Signed out" screen after you log out, it now shows a Restart Beebo button, so you are no longer stuck with greyed-out boxes. A new sign-in still cannot start until the old sign-out has finished.
- Closing and restarting: when Windows shuts down, restarts or signs you out, Beebo now runs its normal closing steps first. When Beebo restarts itself (after you choose your own converter in Playback settings, from the connection checker, or from the Restart Beebo button), it now closes the normal way too. If "Start before sign-in" and "Start with Windows" are both on, the window no longer pops open at every sign-in. With no tray icon, closing the window now minimises Beebo so you can still reach it.
- Starting up: if another program is using Beebo's port, Beebo now keeps trying once a minute instead of giving up after about 25 seconds. After the PC wakes from sleep, Beebo checks that its media server is still running and starts it again if needed. The "start before sign-in" task now runs at normal priority, and the first screen unlock after Beebo starts no longer repeats every network check.
- Uninstalling Beebo now also removes its "Start with Windows" entry. Updates keep it.
- Reliability: a long run of repeated errors no longer makes Beebo slower and slower. Beebo's log file can no longer grow without limit when Windows keeps it locked, and lines lost to a full disk are now counted.
- Browser player at home: if the home computer goes to sleep or Beebo restarts during a film, the player now says it is reconnecting and carries on from the same spot when the computer is back, instead of saying the video format cannot play. The installed web app's "Can't reach your Beebo server" page now tries again by itself, so it comes back when the computer wakes. While Beebo is updating, the player keeps your place and stops waiting if you start a different video.
- Easy Mode: turning Easy Mode off now gives back your own sound settings instead of keeping the clearer-dialogue ones. Phones no longer show a bottom tab for a page your layout hides. If a member with Easy Mode on becomes an admin, there is now a "Turn off Easy Mode" button. The Get Help button and its message now grow with the page's text size.
- Phones as speakers: a phone that slept for a long time now reconnects and plays instead of showing "Reconnecting..." forever. "Map the room" now listens long enough to hear the click, no longer waits for a phone that left, and shows the right message while films are still switching. The phone volume slider now covers the full range (-24 to +12 dB) and no longer jumps back while you drag it. Moving a phone to a seat that takes one phone now sends the phone already there to Spare.
- Photos in the browser: the picture frame no longer cuts off the edges of photos in blur and fit modes. "Show more" no longer shows the same photos twice, and switching tabs quickly no longer fills a tab with the wrong photos. On a touch screen, dragging a video's seek bar no longer jumps to another photo. A photo that cannot be shown (for example some HEIC or RAW files) now shows a clear message instead of a blank screen. German Photos text now uses the polite form (Sie).
- Phone photo backup and Space Saver: a backup that picks up where it stopped is no longer refused as "PC disk full" when most of the file is already on the PC, and a phone that asks again while the PC is still finishing a big file no longer sends the whole file again. A Space Saver folder can now show more than its newest 1,500 photos, an unplugged Space Saver drive now says the folder is not available instead of "No backups yet", and a thumbnail that failed half-way is no longer kept broken. Nothing here deletes or moves a photo or video.
- Users: renaming a person now follows the same name rules as adding one, and a blank or refused name says why it was not saved. The Users tab no longer goes blank, and View stats no longer stops working, when the answer from Beebo is not what it expects. The seat sentence now waits for the real seat limit instead of first showing "up to 6".
- Not switched on yet: fixes for Live Rooms (someone who reconnects shows as here again, clearer messages, turning the camera or microphone on later now asks for it) and for tournaments (a wrong number of players gives an error instead of a crash, ties go to the player with fewer losses, a refused change leaves the result untouched). Both features are still off in this version.
- Behind the scenes (no change to how the app works): new and steadier automated checks, including a real measurement of the Strong volume leveler.
- Windows only. The phone app and Beebo Auto are separate releases.
- Automated checks: the full Windows desktop test suite was run on this release's batch of changes before the Log out fix, the tournament fixes and the version number were added: 2,098 test files passed, 1 failed and was then fixed (a count inside a security check), and 34 were skipped because they cannot run on this PC or are opt-in. After the Log out fix and the tournament fixes were added, the 20 test files for sign-in, sign-out, languages and tournaments passed (510 of 510 tests). On the final code, the 30 test files that load the app screen and its What's new list, the touched-file tests and the offline and route-access checks all passed. The Log out fix, which touches sign-out, had two clear code reviews. The signed installer passed its signature, size, converter, connection-helper and language checks. Installed-app checks on a Windows PC on Nov 23, 2026: 3 of 3 passed (logging out, pressing Restart Beebo and signing in again; Beebo restarting itself and coming back with the library; opening Beebo a second time, normally and hidden, without starting a second copy). Not tried yet: the in-app update from 0.1.136, the closing steps when Windows shuts down or signs out, retrying when the port is busy, the check after the PC wakes from sleep, removing the Start with Windows entry on uninstall, the browser player reconnecting after the PC sleeps or Beebo restarts, and the installed web app's offline page retrying by itself. The other changes in this release have not been tried by a person yet.
